summary: Iteration 6 — end-to-end testing of the 4 new modules: (1) Advisor Household Queue with 0-100 score/status/alerts/next_action, (2) Insurance Gap Analysis with Protection Score + Life/LTC/DI tabs, (3) Canadian Tax Engine (projection/RRSP/TFSA/capgains/split), (4) Spouse/Combined owner toggle on Retirement/Debt/CashFlow + extra-field persistence (owner/in_holding_company). Backend: 12/12 new pytest cases pass in /app/backend/tests/test_iter6_advisor_queue.py (TestAdvisorHouseholdQueue: roster returns score/status/alerts/next_action/net_worth/debt for all 3 Nguyen/Okafor/Rossi households, Nguyen score>=Okafor/Rossi, Okafor+Rossi have 'No retirement/insurance' alerts, non-advisor tiers get 403; TestAdvisorPlanRequiresHousehold: POST /plan/debts without household_id -> 400, with household_id=client_a1 -> 200, enterprise -> 403; TestPlanArbitraryFields: owner tag on debts/expenses, in_holding_company+is_rental+rental_income on networth, insurance_type+coverage on insurance all persist via Mongo and are household-scoped). Frontend verified via Playwright over the public preview URL as advisor@compass.ca with client_a1 open: (1) /clients Household Queue renders all 4 stat cards (Households, Book assets, Avg. health score, Need attention) + per-household Card with client-score-* (Nguyen=100 On Track, Okafor=55 / Rossi=55 Needs Review), client-status-*, client-alerts-* (populated for Okafor+Rossi with 'No retirement projection on file' / 'No insurance analysis — protection gap'), client-action-* ('Schedule annual review' / 'Build a retirement projection'), Progress bar, and open-client-* button that drills in. (2) /insurance shows protection-score-value=21 and protection-band='Significant gaps'; Life/LTC/DI tab buttons present; life-gap=$1,090,000, ltc-gap=$300,000, di-gap=$7,313/mo. Adding a $2M life policy via add-insurance-button -> insurance-modal fields (coverage/premium/carrier/insured) -> insurance-save raised protection-score 21->50 and flipped life-gap to 'No gap'. (3) /tax 5 tabs all present; projection tax-total changes with income ($27,768 at $120k -> $79,539 at $250k ON); rrsp-room is 18%*earned ($18,000 at $100k) and caps at $32,490 at $500k; tfsa-room=$102,000; capgains-tax @ $20k gain = $3,716; split-savings for 200k/40k = $8,081. All values recompute reactively. (4) PersonToggle: ret-person-{primary|spouse|combined}, debt-person-*, cashflow-person-* all present on their respective pages. Retirement spouse-prefill works for owners that have retirement_age/desired_income on their profile; spouse Mai Nguyen's profile has no retirement_age/desired_income/pension_type so switching leaves the current values (code falls back to current state via `|| s.retire_age`) — correct behavior but a seed-data limitation.

minor.issue: Spouse owner (Mai Nguyen) has no retirement_age / desired_income / pension_type fields on her owner record, so the Retirement spouse-view prefill is a no-op. Seed could populate these for a better demo.

ui_bugs.issue: client-alerts-<id> div is only rendered when alerts.length>0, so for high-scoring households (Nguyen score=100) the data-testid is absent. Harmless but QA scripts that always expect the testid will see MISSING.

action_items: (Low) Seed Mai Nguyen's owner record with retirement_age / desired_income / pension_type so switching the Retirement toggle to Spouse visibly re-populates the inputs.
(Low) Always render the client-alerts-<id> element (even if empty) so automation can assert on it; or document that absence==no alerts.
(Nice) Previously flagged: pyotp 30s rotation race under xdist for legacy suites — still present; new iter6 suite regenerates code immediately before each verify to avoid it.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py _household_score(): simple deterministic scoring is fine for a demo but net_worth negative penalty + no-retirement + no-insurance can stack unbounded if more criteria are added — consider explicit weight table.

server.py plan_create/update/delete: `if user['tier']=='advisor' and not hid: 400` is good; same guard missing on PUT /plan/profile? plan_profile_save still allows advisor to update profile without household_id (would then write to no particular household — a cross-household leak risk since planner_scope filters are read-side only). Worth verifying.

Insurance.jsx: Protection Score is computed client-side from policies+income+dependants+debt. Mutating one tab's policies updates it immediately — good. No server-side analysis endpoint, which matches the 'illustrative only' spec but means scoring differs if the frontend is bypassed.
tax.js: client-side 2025 Canadian brackets are hardcoded — if 2026 brackets change, this will drift silently. Add a comment linking to the CRA source and a year constant.

Retirement.jsx applyPerson: falls back to current state when owner profile lacks fields (`Number(p.retirement_age || s.retire_age)`) — this means a toggle click can silently be a no-op. Prefer explicit null-state so the UI can show 'no profile data'.
AdvisorClients.jsx: client-alerts-<id> div only rendered when alerts.length>0 — makes automated assertions brittle.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on all 4 feature areas: Household Queue, Insurance (Protection Score + 3 tabs + add-policy increases score), Tax (5 tabs, all computations reactive incl. RRSP cap), Person toggle present on Retirement/Debt/CashFlow
